title: Adaptive microbatch presets and KV-warmup heuristics with unit-econ prober
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Background: Customers running latency-sensitive LLM endpoints often over-provision small batch sizes to meet 99th percentile SLOs which increases per-token cost. Separately, cold KV cache misses for multi-turn chat impose a tail-latency penalty that pushes teams to keep higher headroom or run less aggressive quantization. This PR introduces an end-to-end feature: (1) adaptive microbatch presets exposed as route defaults, (2) a lightweight KV-warmup heuristic that uses request-side prefix probing to prefill caches for hot sessions, and (3) a non-invasive Unit-Econ Prober service that injects low-rate synthetic probes to estimate per-route cost/latency curves used to pick microbatch and warmup presets.

Summary of changes: Adds a new runtime hook + controller and a Console UI flag to enable adaptive-presets per-route. Implements the Unit-Econ Prober as a standalone internal controller that schedules probes based on traffic heatmaps and returns JSON summaries consumed by the heuristics engine. Updates serving runtime to accept microbatch-presets and a cache-prefill window parameter. Adds telemetry (per-probe token cost, p50/p95 latency, KV-prefill hit-rate). Includes a migration tool to backfill presets from historical per-route traces.

Motivation: Prior work (frugal batching and autotuners) optimizes at global or per-model granularity; teams asked for safer route-level defaults that are cheap to compute and can be toggled without full traffic experiments. The prober lets us measure realistic unit economics in-cluster without affecting customer payloads, while the KV-warmup materially reduces tail latency on multi-turn sessions where conversational state is reused.

Design highlights:
- Microbatch presets: a small enum (none, conservative, balanced, aggressive) plus per-route numeric override. The presets translate to target batch size, max latency window, and max async in-flight requests. The runtime schedules a microbatch delta scheduler that tries to reach the preset without violating latency SLOs.
- KV-warmup heuristic: samples incoming request prefixes for active sessions and issues low-priority prefill requests using the same model variant. Prefill concurrency is capped per-route and backpressure-aware (won't prefill if CPU/GPU utilization > threshold).
- Unit-Econ Prober: generates 1–5 probe requests per minute per hot route (configurable) with synthetic but realistic prefixes (derived from anonymized recent traffic). Prober returns a compact profile: p50/p95 tokens/sec, cost-per-token, inferred break-even batch size. These profiles are stored as route annotations consumed by the presets controller.

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/scheduler/microbatch.go (scheduler + presets implementation)
- runtime/caching/kv_warmup.go (prefill client + heuristics)
- controllers/unit_econ/prober_controller.go (prober logic + metrics collector)
- api/routes/types.go (route presets schema + validation)
- console/src/routes/RouteSettings.tsx (toggle and summary UI)
- telemetry/metrics/unit_econ.prom (new meters)
- migrations/20260215_backfill_presets.go (backfill job)
- tests/e2e/prober_integration_test.go
- docs/operational/route-presets.md

Small code excerpt (microbatch policy application):
```
// targetWindowMillis derived from preset
scheduler.SetTargetWindow(routeID, targetWindowMillis)
// runtime will attempt to form batches within target window up to maxBatchSize
```

Testing and benchmarks: Unit and integration tests added. Benchmarked on the perf-lab using a 4-model mix (chat, completion, rerank, embedding) across 8 GPU backends. Key numbers from canary cluster: conservative preset reduced cost by 6.2% vs default while holding p95 latency within 1.1x; aggressive preset reduced cost by 17.8% but increased p95 by 1.45x on tail-heavy workloads. KV-warmup decreased session tail p95 by 18% for multi-turn chat flows with average session length >6 turns.

CI: initial run failed lint due to a naming inconsistency in proto; lint-only commit was pushed and CI passed on rerun. End-to-end test showed a flaky case in prefill backpressure—added a retry/backoff and fixed.

Migration and rollout plan: feature default off. Deploy prober controller and metrics in canary region, enable presets UI for internal teams only, run the backfill migration to seed sensible defaults. After 2 weeks of monitoring (unit-econ signals + console charts) we will flip the defaults to "balanced" for routes tagged with 'autotune-eligible'. Rollout is reversible: presets are per-route overrides and can be disabled immediately.

Rollback: remove route annotations and revert controller feature flag. Migration is idempotent and a reverse job exists to clear seeded presets.

Security and privacy: Probes use anonymized prefixes derived from sampled tokens and conform to the data retention policy; probes do not include user-identifiable metadata. Prober runs with restricted IAM roles and KMS usage consistent with Private deployment rules.

Open items and follow-ups:
- Add automatic quantization recommendation integration (next PR) to suggest int8 profiles when latencies allow.
- Expand probe synthesis logic to better model long-tail conversation styles.
- Expose detailed cost/latency curve plotting in Console (UX ticket PM-329).

Related work: refs ENG-8473 (microbatch scheduling improvements), PM-312 (route-level defaults), and prior perf canaries PRs for KV cache improvements.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] Perf numbers from lab
- [x] Console UI with toggle
- [x] Migration/backfill job

Merge notes: squash + reword. See migration job schedule in release notes.

feat(kv): implement warmup prefill client with backpressure
feat(prober): unit-econ prober controller and metrics
chore(console): add route presets UI and summaries
test(e2e): prober integration scenarios and migration backfill
perf(tune): reduce prefill concurrency and add retry/backoff
review_comments: Miguel: Can we ensure prober rate cannot amplify and become a DoS? Author: prober uses leaky-bucket and route caps, added in code.
Lena: Why not use historical traces instead of synthetic probes? Author: historical traces are used for synthesis seeds but probes are needed to measure live unit-econ under current infra.
Rajesh: Will prefill increase GPU usage? Author: capped by route and global thresholds; scheduler respects util metrics and will disable prefill under high utilization.
release_notes:
- Add adaptive microbatch presets (route-level)
- Add KV-warmup prefill heuristic to reduce tail latency on multi-turn sessions
- Add Unit-Econ Prober to estimate per-route cost/latency tradeoffs and seed presets
- Backfill migration to seed presets from historical traces
